classes.name: Triptans
classes.description: Acute migraine 5-HT1B/1D agonists: sumatriptan (tablet, nasal, injection; Imitrex, Tosymra, Zembrace), rizatriptan (Maxalt, MLT), zolmitriptan (Zomig), eletriptan (Relpax), naratriptan, almotriptan, frovatriptan, sumatriptan/naproxen (Treximet).
classes.plainDescription: A pill (or spray/shot) taken when a migraine starts.

classes.name: Acute CGRP antagonists (gepants) & ditans
classes.description: Acute CGRP receptor antagonists and ditans: rimegepant (Nurtec ODT, also preventive), ubrogepant (Ubrelvy), zavegepant nasal (Zavzpret), lasmiditan (Reyvow).
classes.plainDescription: A newer migraine pill (or nasal spray) for when triptans don't work or aren't safe.

classes.name: CGRP preventives

classes.plainDescription: A monthly shot (or daily pill) that prevents migraines.

Preferred pick = sumatriptan (judgment: most-used generic triptan with no PA). Other Tier 1 triptans are QL-only, so they are alternatives. Frovatriptan, sumatriptan-naproxen, the sumatriptan subcutaneous refill and auto-injector, and brand Zomig carry ST; QL (p. 64) and go in paRequired as step barriers. Eletriptan and sumatriptan subcutaneous are Tier 2 QL. Dihydroergotamine products are outside this class.

Emgality appears on three lines (prefilled syringe '300 mg dose', auto-injector, prefilled syringe), all Tier 2 PA; QL. The 300 mg line is the cluster-headache presentation; the list does not state strength for the other two lines, so the 120 mg migraine dose is standard label dosing. Erenumab (Aimovig), fremanezumab (Ajovy), eptinezumab (Vyepti, IV) and atogepant (Qulipta, oral) are absent; complete-listing statement p. 2. Topiramate tablet (p. 18) is a single-agent generic, not a CGRP agent, and is not counted here. [Sonnet check 2026-10-21: Eptinezumab (Vyepti, IV infusion) removed from paRequired: provider-administered (medical benefit), not a pharmacy-list exclusion. Aimovig, Ajovy and Qulipta are pharmacy products, so their nonformulary status stays.]
